story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Isn't that amazing? And Louis Armstrong, the same way. The most horrible -- all through his life, I remember I listened to those bands and they were just horrible. And he was blowing this most beautiful stuff (inaudible).
He liked the saxophone. He liked Guy
Lombardo's saxophones, and my God, he had them. God, they were awful.
Yeah, they were out of tune, they played terrible.
But did you notice, when Louis came in it would be bang, he pulled the whole band together. It was just all of a sudden, it would be heaven.

It was amazing, all through (inaudible). Listen, even those old -- even the ones back as far as King Oliver, when Louis -- they'd be just trumping along, just dying, and all of a sudden Louis would start swinging and everything was perfect.
"I Can't Believe in Love," (inaudible) the band going, you know (humming), and the band goes (Humming). You know, the band is together.
And the classic of Louis Armstrong is "Strutting With Some Barbeque." And that sax -- that clarinet player should be shot.
Oh, yeah, that was a great favorite. (Humming).
But everybody used to sit around and just cringe. And then Louis played such a great solo on that.
Oh, that was a good record.
Good record, and this clarinet player just destroyed it.
Yeah, that was just the time everybody had buried Louis, said he's through, he's lost his chops, you know. And oh, this dynamite record came out.
